page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head "DESCRIPTIO" centred above the text, page number 44 at the top left. Catchword "mus" at the bottom right. No marginal notes. Library stamps at the bottom left and the edge of the neighbouring page at the right are left out.

main_text.p: go in intimo sinu magno, peninsulae simi-lis. Cervix enim eam a continente se-parabat lata xxv stadia. Ab eâ cervi-ce lingua quadam oblonga semistadium lata, excurrebat versus occidentem inter stagnum & mare, rupibus undique mu-nita, & muro simplice. Versus meridiem & continentem, ubi etiam Byrsa erat in cervice, murus triplex erat, altus xxx cubitos absque propugnaculis & turri-bus, quae binorum jugerum spacis inter se distabant per circuitum, nixa funda-mentis xxx pedum, singula contignatio-num quatuor. Muri vero ad secundam contignationem pertingebant. Erant autem fornicati & capaces, in quorum infima parte ccc elephanti stabulabantur, adjunctis pabuli promptuariis. Superius erant quatuor millium equorum stabula cum hordei penuariis. Virorum quoque diversoria xx millium peditum, quatuor millium equitum. Tantus apparatus bellicus ordinarium locum habebat in solis mœnibus. Angulus autem, qui ab hoc muro praeter dictam linguam ad portus flectebatur, solus erat debilis & humilis, neglectus a principio. Hi portus sic erant dispositi, ut navigatio esset ex alio in alium, & ab alto unum commune os patebat latum pedes lxx, quod claudebatur catenis ferreis. Pri-

page.notes: Right page edge and bottom-left stamps are not printed text and were left out. The word "Byrsa" and the line-end word "mœnibus" were read from a small scan; the "œ" in "mœnibus" is a best reading. Where the text reads "spacis", the printed form is "spacijs"; it was normalised as the vowel i. The word "Pri-" at the foot continues as "Primus" in the catchword.
